questions.q: What three steps does Quartuccio recommend for escaping a life that feels stuck?
a: Awakening, disrupting and designing
Planning, saving and retiring
Learning, networking and negotiating
Accepting, enduring and adapting
questions.why: Lesson 1 lays out the three stages, starting with waking up to your current patterns.

questions.q: What does the awakening stage involve?
a: Using mindfulness to notice the habits that keep you stuck
Quitting your job before making any plans
Asking friends to choose a new career for you
Setting a strict deadline for your next promotion
questions.why: Lesson 1 says you observe your actions and focus on what makes you unhappy.

questions.q: Why does visualizing your future self help motivate change?
a: We picture our future selves almost like strangers, so seeing a bad outcome shocks us
The brain treats future plans as already achieved
Visualization removes all risk from a career change
It replaces the need for any daily habits
questions.why: Lesson 2 cites brain scans showing future selves feel distant, which makes a vivid picture powerful.

questions.q: How does a daily scorecard help you pursue a goal?
a: Seeing accumulated successful days builds confidence and softens single slip-ups
It punishes every missed day with a financial penalty
It compares your progress with that of your friends
It replaces the need to set any long-term goals
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a streak of completed days makes one failure look small.

questions.q: What evening rituals does the summary suggest for setting up a good day?
a: Limiting devices, meditating and planning the next day
Reviewing email until you feel sleepy
Working late to finish every unfinished task
Watching television to switch off completely
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends these habits to make evenings effective rather than draining.
